q-1780.name: Question 1
q-1780.problem: Suppose you have $5$ shirts, $4$ pants, and $9$ ties. How many outfits can be made consisting of a shirt, pants, and a tie?
q-1780.worked_solution:
Using the **rule of product**, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Number of outfits} & =\text{Number of shirts} \\  & \times \text{Number of pants} \\  & \times \text{Number of ties} \\  & =5\times 4\times 9 \\  & =180.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $180$ different outfits can be made consisting of a shirt, pants, and a tie.

q-1805.name: Question 2
q-1805.problem:
A word consists of $4$ letters, as shown below:

| Letter | Letter | Letter | Letter |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Here, each "Letter" can be any capital from A-Z ($26$ in total). How many possible words are there?
q-1805.worked_solution:
For each letter, there is a total of $26$ possibilities.

Using the **rule of product**, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Number of words} & =\text{Number of options in the first slot} \\  & \times \text{Number of options in the second slot} \\  & \times \text{Number of options in the third slot} \\  & \times \text{Number of options in the fourth slot} \\  & =26\times 26\times 26\times 26 \\  & ={26}^{4} \\  & =456\,976.\end{aligned}
$$

So, there are $456\,976$ possible words.

q-5552.name: Question 3
q-5552.problem:
John has $3$ pants, $5$ shirts, and $6$ pairs of socks.
If John wears one pair of pants, one shirt, and one matching pair of socks, how many different combinations of outfits can he wear?
q-5552.worked_solution:
Using the **rule of product**, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Number of outfits} & =\text{Number of pants} \\  & \times \text{Number of shirts} \\  & \times \text{Number of pairs of socks} \\  & =3\times 5\times 6 \\  & =90.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, John can dress in $90$ different ways.
